clue.text: Superior boat at sea rounding first of buoys

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the jumbled letters wrap the single letter
something at sea is adrift and confused, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: the fodder to be jumbled

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the initial letter of buoys

explanation.surface: A fine vessel sails out, circling a marker buoy.
explanation.walkthrough: ABOT, the shuffled boat, takes B after its first letter to give ABBOT. 'Superior' here is a noun: the head of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of a monastery, and a monastic head is called a superior.

clue.text: Biblical character very good graduate raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: so good means very good, and SO alone carries the 'very'
a Master of Arts is a graduate

explanation.surface: A saintly figure from scripture who was also a university graduate gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: SO plus MA makes SOMA, which read upwards gives AMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is an Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: Killed brutally, the cur, surprisingly in bed

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, then split around the jumble

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dog was found savagely slain in its bed, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher someone is to slaughter them savagely, like an animal in an abattoir.

clue.text: The serious fight is about to begin, gauntlets having been thrown down?

definitions.text: The serious fight is about to begin
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for when hostilities get earnest
second meaning, literal: the hand coverings have been removed

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from boxing, where fighting bare-fisted signals real violence; the question mark flags the literal second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals that restraint is abandoned and real conflict starts; literally, the protective handwear has been removed.

clue.text: Result of fine season

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A sunny spell produces a good outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are the product of breeding, and figuratively any result or outcome of something.

clue.text: Boring old Lew turned in sick

parts.note: O is a common abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in places the flipped name inside the word for unwell

parts.note: sick means ill; it is split around the name

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Tedious old Lew has fallen ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like an adjective for dull Lew, but it is a noun: a hole drilled into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A boring is a shaft drilled into the earth, and an oil well is exactly such a drilled shaft.

clue.text: Plant, unrestrained, is climbing onto roof of attic

parts.note: unrestrained means free

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the little word is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards

indicators.note: the roof is the top of a down entry's word, so its first letter is wanted

parts.note: the top letter of attic

explanation.surface: A plant grows wild and climbs up to the attic roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant grown from corms, popular as a cut flower.

clue.text: Blacklisted pro, I suspect, is game

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A banned professional player is under suspicion, the speaker thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket billiards is a cue game, another name for pool, played on a table with pockets.

clue.text: Unsuitable home, small apartment

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
apt. is the short form of apartment

explanation.surface: A tiny flat is no good as a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-suited, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Don hit, then treated

parts.note: to get someone can mean to strike them, as in 'the punch got him on the chin'
a wound is dressed when it is treated and bandaged

explanation.surface: A university lecturer was struck and needed medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but here it is the verb meaning to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothing is to put it on, which is what you do when you clothe yourself in the morning.

clue.text: Stir me a lot, a porridge

indicators.note: to stir is to mix things around, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A cook is told to give the porridge a good stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, and in American usage the word names the cooked breakfast dish of porridge itself.

clue.text: Captivate audience, at the end, with new song

indicators.note: at the end points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of audience
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A singer wins the crowd over at the close of the show with a fresh number.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or delight, holding someone's attention as if by a spell.

clue.text: In disorder, slide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a hurried, confused manner
second meaning: a tall spiral slide at a fairground

explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is a British fairground ride: a tower with a slide spiralling round the outside, ridden on a mat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes chaotic haste, and the noun names a spiral fairground slide.

clue.text: Informer, good and bent?

parts.note: super means very good
bent is a type of grass, common on lawns

explanation.surface: Is the police informant honest, or crooked?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked, fitting an informer, but it is the name of a grass. In British slang a supergrass is a criminal who informs on many associates.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass is British slang for a police informant; a supergrass betrays a large number of fellow criminals.

clue.text: Straighten out a French composer

parts.note: un is French for a
Maurice Ravel, composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: Someone sets a French composer straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a tangle is to undo it, so sorting out or clearing up a muddle.

clue.text: Evergreen Arabian? On the contrary, American

parts.note: Ar. is a dictionary abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
but introduces a contrary statement
US stands for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: Is this evergreen plant from Arabia? No, from America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question and answer, but each phrase supplies a piece in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen shrub or small tree with red berries.

clue.text: Giant, dear comic actor

indicators.note: comic means funny or ridiculous, so the letters are made to clown about into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge, lovable comedy performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic actor' looks like the definition, but a comic actor is the opposite of the answer: only 'actor' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Sender nervous about uranium's ultimate consumer

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumble surrounds the chemical symbol
a nervous person is jittery and jumbled, so the word before it is mixed up

parts.note: the fodder to be rearranged
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Someone posting a radioactive parcel frets about whether it will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the person who finally uses a product, the last consumer in the supply chain.

clue.text: Royal Engineers go, reportedly, to raise a siege

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Army engineers are said to be departing to break a blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a besieged town is to free it by driving off the attackers.

clue.text: Drink from bucket? Feel unwell, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are listened to, so their sound counts, not their spelling

parts.note: a pail is a bucket
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Drinking from a bucket would make anyone feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale ale is a light-coloured beer brewed with pale malt.

clue.text: Threw tar over editor

parts.note: pitch is black tar
ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone flung tar all over a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, one piece over another means it sits above, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a ball is to throw it, so pitched is the past tense meaning threw.

clue.text: Army officer has to attack nationwide walkout

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
to strike is to attack

explanation.surface: A senior commander must launch an assault during a national stoppage.
explanation.definitionFit: A general strike is a coordinated stoppage of work by workers across a whole country.

clue.text: The head on the French gold coin, now obsolete

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A king's head appears on an old French gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble was a medieval English gold coin, long out of circulation.

clue.text: Small piece of jewellery getting endless attention

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: study is close attention

explanation.surface: A tiny jewel attracts unceasing notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small earring or ornament with a post, a little piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Saint featured in some bar that's prejudiced

indicators.note: prejudiced means biased or bent away from the true line, so the letters are warped into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint turns up in a pub where the drinkers are bigoted.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ambrose was the fourth-century bishop of Milan, one of the four Latin Doctors of the Church.

clue.text: Hit rear, upsetting girl

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A smack on the bottom upsets a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet is a girl's name, and crosswords often define first names as boy or girl.

clue.text: Book by female, Irish composer from this city

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
F is the abbreviation for female
John Field, Irish composer who invented the nocturne

explanation.surface: A novel by a woman and an Irish composer both come from this city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is not a general word for a book but a specific title: She, the Victorian adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a city in South Yorkshire, England, famous for steel.

clue.text: Church council, somewhat busy no doubt

indicators.note: somewhat means only to a degree, so just part of the phrase is used

parts.note: the letters run across busy, no and doubt

explanation.surface: The church committee is rather busy, no doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church officials that governs church affairs.
